subject: Deployment choice recap — Hosted / Dedicated / Private & migration options
body:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Reilly <sara.reilly@finpay.com>; Alex Tremblay <alex.tremblay@finpay.com>
Cc: procurement@finpay.com
Date: Mon, 11 Oct 2026 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Deployment choice recap — Hosted / Dedicated / Private & migration options

Hi Sara / Alex — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we all stay aligned: 

Summary of their priorities (from call):
- Hard latency requirement: 100ms p95 for inference on short prompts (<=128 tokens).
- Data residency: production customer data must remain in US regions; future EU expansion possible.
- Security: SOC 2 evidence and KMS integration required for keys.
- Migration: currently using OldAI's hosted API for most traffic; a small portion runs on an on-prem legacy GPU cluster for sensitive workloads.

Options we discussed:
1) Hosted API (fastest ramp): lowest integration friction, managed keys, but multi-tenant; can meet latency for baseline workloads with proper routing and caching.
2) Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pool): predictable throughput, burst option, and isolated GPU instances we can reserve for FinPay — good tradeoff for consistent latency and cost predictability.
3) Private (VPC / on-prem): full network isolation, customer-managed VPC and KMS; longer lead time (network / security onboarding) but required for regulated flows.

Migration considerations we highlighted:
- From OldAI hosted API: we can set up dual-write/dual-read probes and use prefix caching to preserve warm KV caches as you flip traffic; usually low lift.
- From your legacy GPU cluster: requires model conversion (we support standard PyTorch + TorchScript + quantized variants), plus cooldown for KV migration; timeline depends on model size and custom ops.

Proposed immediate next steps:
- Provide a short fingerprint of traffic (QPS by endpoint, average and 95th percentile token lengths, peak concurrency) — Sara, can you send that by end of day Wed?
- I will loop in Ben (solutions engineer) to give a quick Dedicated sizing estimate and outline Private onboarding checklist.
- If procurement is ready, I’ll prepare a 6‑week Dedicated POC SOW (DocuSign link) and a parallel checklist for Private handoff if you choose to pursue that later.

Attachments: FinPay_Migration_Comparison.xlsx (brief cost/latency delta), SOC2-evidence-stub.pdf (what we can provide), dedicated-sizing-proposal.xlsx (placeholder).

Thanks — talk soon.

Best,
Karthik
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0119

From: Sara Reilly <sara.reilly@finpay.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alex Tremblay <alex.tremblay@finpay.com>; procurement@finpay.com
Date: Tue, 12 Oct 2026 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Deployment choice recap — Hosted / Dedicated / Private & migration options

Thanks Karthik — helpful recap. A few clarifications and ask: 

1) Latency: the 100ms p95 target applies to our fraud scoring endpoint which has short prompts (~60 tokens) and must be <=100ms p95. For longer context flows (customer support, 1k tokens), higher p95 is acceptable.
2) Traffic footprint: currently ~80 rps to OldAI's hosted endpoints during peak, with steady-state 30 rps. Average prompt length is ~220 tokens; fraud endpoint is 60 tokens.
3) Legacy on-prem cluster: 4xV100 machines running a custom serving wrapper. We want to retire that within 6 months but need an option to keep highly sensitive traffic on-prem until we complete compliance sign-offs.
4) Procurement: can you include an option for a Dedicated reservation with burst capacity and an addendum outlining the Private onboarding timeline and costs?

Also: can Ben confirm whether we would need model rework to be compatible with Redwood's faster attention kernels? Our inference is currently custom CUDA ops on top of PyTorch.

Sara
Sara Reilly
VP, Platform Engineering | FinPay

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>

Subject: Fwd: Deployment choice recap — Hosted / Dedicated / Private & migration options

Internal — forwarding the FinPay clarifications. High level ask: can we put together the following by EOD Thurs so I can send to procurement?
- Dedicated sizing + cost table (include burst option) based on peak 80 rps, token mixes (60 tokens fraud vs 220 tokens average).
- Private onboarding timeline and milestone checklist (network peering, KMS integration, audit evidence handoff).
- Technical note on compatibility: what is the likely level of model rework for their custom CUDA ops? Any recommended migration steps (model conversion, quantization, fallback strategy).

Vanessa — can you draft the procurement-facing SOW outline (6-week Dedicated POC + option to convert to Private) and attach a high-level SLO/SLA appendix?

Thanks — Karthik

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sara Reilly <sara.reilly@finpay.com>, Alex Tremblay <alex.tremblay@finpay.com>, procurement@finpay.com
Date: Tue, 12 Oct 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Deployment choice recap — Hosted / Dedicated / Private & migration options

Thanks for the details — quick technical readout and asks: 

Compatibility note:
- Redwood supports standard PyTorch models and common CUDA ops. Custom CUDA wrappers can be the sticking point; we typically do one of: 1) upstream the op to a supported kernel, 2) provide a thin shim so the model runs under our runtime, or 3) run those ops in a dedicated private lane (if Private deployment).

Estimated effort:
- If they can provide a model artifact (PyTorch + example inputs), we can assess in ~3 business days. For heavy custom ops expect 2–4 weeks for engineering work to either shim or port.

Sizing (initial Dedicated estimate for peak 80 rps):
- Fraud endpoint (60 tokens, 80 rps peak): 2x A40s reserved with autoscale to 4x for bursts (expected p95 ~85–95ms with continuous batching and warm prefix cache).
- Main traffic (avg 220 tokens, 30 rps steady): 1x A40 reserved; autoscale to 2x for growth.
- Cost delta vs Hosted (per-token): Dedicated reduces per-token cost ~35% for sustained traffic but requires reserve commitment.

Private considerations:
- Network onboarding: VPC peering + customer firewall rules; expect 3–4 week lead time from paperwork sign-off.
- KMS/HSM: we support external KMS keys; integration and key rotation policy review required (2 weeks).
- Audit: we can provide SOC2 artifacts and evidence package (attached stub).

Migration plan sketch (for proposal):
1) Discovery: ingest models & test artifacts (3 business days).
2) Compatibility pass: run model in our runtime, note custom ops (3–10 business days depending on complexity).
3) POC on Dedicated: 6 weeks — includes load tests, latency tuning, KV-warm runs, and cutover rehearsals.
4) Private cutover (optional): 3–6 weeks after SOC/KMS onboarding.

Questions for FinPay (Sara / Alex):
- Can you share example model artifacts and a small traffic dump (1 hour) we can run in our testbed?
- Any hard freeze windows or compliance blackout periods in the next 90 days?

I’ll attach a short Dedicated-sizing workbook (dedicated-sizing-proposal.xlsx) and a succinct migration-comparison (FinPay_Migration_Comparison.xlsx).

-Ben
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai

Appreciate the detail — good plan. We want to move forward with a 6-week Dedicated POC with the following requirements: 
- Include burst capacity up to +150% for Black Week testing;
- KMS integration documented in the SOW;
- Private onboarding checklist included as an optional follow-on (we expect to decide on Private after the POC).

Procurement note: procurement@finpay.com is on copy. Sara, please prepare the small traffic dump and an example model bundle by EOD Friday. Alex will review the technical compatibility once Ben has the initial assessment.

Please prepare a draft SOW and the DocuSign-ready paperwork (I see the link in related links) and I’ll route it internally for signature. Budget has been tentatively approved for a Dedicated trial.

Thanks — Sara
